29 A beam of light consists of two wavelengths of 436 nm and 654 nm. A diffraction grating of
5.00 × 105 lines m–1 produces a diffraction pattern in which the second order of one of these
wavelengths occurs at the same angle θ as the third order of the other wavelength.
overlapping orders
zero order
436 nm
654 nm
θ
θ
What is the angle θ ?
A
19.1°
B
25.8°
C
40.8°
D
78.8°

hints: Notice the two wavelengths $436 \text{ nm}$ and $654 \text{ nm}$ and that $654$ is $1.5$ times $436$, so check which $2\lambda$ equals which $3\lambda$.
Recall the grating equation $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ and that overlapping means $n_1\lambda_1 = n_2\lambda_2$ at the same $\theta$.
First find the slit spacing from $d = 1/N$ with $N = 5.00 \times 10^5 \text{ m}^{-1}$, then use $\sin\theta = n\lambda/d$ with the overlapping $n = 2$ and $\lambda = 654 \text{ nm}$.
walkthrough: Find the grating spacing from the lines per metre: $d = 1/N = 1/(5.00 \times 10^5 \text{ m}^{-1}) = 2.00 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$.

Check the overlap condition: $2 \times 654 \text{ nm} = 1308 \text{ nm}$ and $3 \times 436 \text{ nm} = 1308 \text{ nm}$, so the second order of $654 \text{ nm}$ overlaps the third order of $436 \text{ nm}$.
Apply the diffraction grating equation $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ using either overlapping pair, for example $n = 2$ and $\lambda = 654 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$.
Calculate the angle: $\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.654) = 40.8^{\circ}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is too small and would correspond to using $n=1$ with $436 \text{ nm}$ in $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$.

B.explanation: This is too small and would correspond to using $n=1$ with $654 \text{ nm}$ in $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$.

C.explanation: Both $2 \times 654 \text{ nm}$ and $3 \times 436 \text{ nm}$ equal $1308 \text{ nm}$, giving $\sin\theta = 0.654$ and $\theta = 40.8^{\circ}$.

D.explanation: This is too large and cannot be obtained from $d \sin\theta = n\lambda$ with the overlapping $n\lambda = 1308 \text{ nm}$.
